results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate is a digital record that attests to an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic integrity hash (SHA-256) that makes any tampering detectable, and hashes are additionally anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time. 

Anyone can verify a certificate without an account using its QR code or by tapping a phone against an attached Attesté NFC tag. For artist-made works, the record begins at creation with a First Witness source certificate, and unlimited certificates are included from the Collector tier up.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A source certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued by you, the artist, directly from your studio at the moment of creation. It is the gold-standard provenance record—confirming authorship at the point of origin and serving as the first link in the chain that a collector carries forward. 

It is different because every later record links back to it. Instead of provenance being reconstructed years later from fading paper, a source certificate is recorded forward from the source, cryptographically signed, and hash-verified so that tampering is instantly detectable. 

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the origin of an artwork's provenance chain, created when an artist registers a new work on Attesté at the moment of making. It is the artist's own recorded account in their own voice, SHA-256-sealed and Bitcoin-anchored. 

Because it is recorded at creation by the maker rather than reconstructed years later from surviving paper, it serves as the foundation every later record builds on and can never be backfilled. It provides the strongest possible starting point a work can carry forward into every collector's portfolio.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
Attesté NFC tags act as a physical handshake between an artwork and its digital provenance. Once a physical NFC tag is bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation, anyone can simply tap a phone against the tag to open the certificate's verification view. 

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. A few tips if a tag isn't reading: make sure NFC is enabled on your device, move the phone slowly over the tag (as the antenna is at the top edge of most phones), remove thick cases, and avoid metal surfaces directly behind the tag. Please note that NFC requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across your collection, your gallery, and your studio practice to handle the heavy lifting of cataloguing, discovery, and marketing. 

Here is what the AI actually does across the platform:

- **Atelier (Voice & Vision Companion):** You can point your camera at an artwork and talk to it in real time. Atelier sees what you see, answers questions about style, technique, and provenance aloud, and automatically saves every session as a journal entry pinned to the work. It also helps artists and collectors draft artwork descriptions from photos.
- **AI Art Sommelier:** It builds a taste profile based on your collection and activity, then recommends exhibitions, galleries, and discoveries matched to your aesthetic. 
- **AI Art Scout:** When you photograph any artwork, the vision AI instantly identifies the likely artist, medium, and period with an honest confidence score.
- **Condition Analysis:** It guides you through multi-angle photos of a work to draft a condition assessment, building a condition history over time for your insurance vault.
- **For Galleries (Almanac and AI Writers):** Almanac is an AI business copilot that answers questions grounded in your live inventory, exhibitions, and pipeline. Galleries also get AI-drafted exhibition copy, artist bios, artwork descriptions, collector follow-up email drafts, social posts, artist reports, and Gallery Wrapped—an annual story of your gallery's year.
- **AI Trail Generator:** It creates custom walking trails with curated stops, descriptions, and GPS coordinates based on your interests and region.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/help/gallery-tools, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/galleries

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account directly inside the app: go to Profile, open Settings, scroll to Account, and tap Delete account. Type DELETE in capital letters to confirm, and your account and data will be removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can also request deletion by emailing info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account". Deleting your account is permanent and cannot be undone, so you may want to export your data first from Settings under Privacy. Please note that deleting your account does not automatically cancel any active store subscription, so you will need to cancel that separately through Apple or Google settings.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/account-and-data

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers a built-in AI assistant (Atelier), a genuine free tier (Explorer) with no credit card required, native mobile apps for iOS and Android, cryptographic SHA-256 provenance with NFC, and provenance recorded at creation via First Witness. In contrast, Artwork Archive is web-only with no native mobile app, does not have a permanently free plan (offering a 14-day trial instead), and has no built-in AI assistant or native AI features.

For pricing, Attesté's unlimited collector plan is $19.99/month, whereas Artwork Archive's top collector plan runs roughly $36–42/month. However, Artwork Archive has a 15-year track record and mature features like consignment management, public collection pages, a Discovery marketplace, and a Call-for-Entry board, which Attesté does not offer.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
